title: Schema Bridge: compatibility and streaming-constrained smoke suite
creator: Aisha Khan
description: We need a focused smoke test suite (Schema Bridge) that validates JSON mode enforcement and constrained-decoder behavior across streaming responses and function/tool-calling interactions. Unlike previous extensive regression harnesses, this ticket scopes a lightweight, fast-to-run smoke battery that: 1) exercises partial/late-arriving tokens and sentinel/toolcall interleaving, 2) validates schema adherence and graceful fallback under token-loss or truncation, and 3) verifies compatibility rules when routing requests to different model variants (quantized, fp16, smaller family). The harness should be runnable in CI (fast) and locally by engineers/debuggers (deterministic seeds), produce clear pass/fail metrics, and emit artifacts useful for triage (example traces, minimal failing prompt set, and a replay fixture).
acceptance_criteria: CI job 'ci/schema-bridge-smoke' runs in < 12 mins and completes on the main branch
Non-adversarial golden prompts show schema adherence >= 99% across supported model variants (base, quantized, fp16) as measured by strict JSON-mode validator

When simulated streaming loss (random chunk drop up to 8%) is applied, the constrained decoder should either produce a valid fallback JSON or flag a deterministic parse-failure with a clear error code (SCHEMA_BRIDGE_PARTIAL).

Tool/function call interleaving: when the model emits a tool call mid-stream, the reconstructor must produce a consistent tool payload in >= 98% of runs; failures must include the raw token stream for replay.
Smoke suite produces a compact failure artifact (max 200KB) with prompt, model config, token-level trace, and validator output for every failing test case.
test_plan: Build a small harness that drives the Redwood API with streaming=true + json_mode enforced, supporting three model variants: 'rwd-base', 'rwd-quant-8', 'rwd-fp16'.
Implement simulated network/stream conditions: token-drop (configurable percentage), out-of-order chunk delivery, and truncated final chunk. Record token indices and timing metadata.

Add tool/function call scenarios: tool call emitted exactly at chunk boundary, tool call spanning multiple chunks, and tool call followed by extra partial JSON payload. Validate tool payload reconstruction.
Run deterministic seed-based generation for 120 golden prompts (mix of trivial and structured scenarios) and 30 adversarial prompts crafted to provoke schema drift.
Instrument validator to produce concise labels: PASS, SOFT_FAIL (relaxation required), HARD_FAIL (invalid JSON), PARTIAL_FAIL (stream truncated).
Expose a CLI wrapper 'schema-bridge-run --ci' that runs the smoke suite and uploads artifacts to the test-bucket and triggers a GitHub check via ci/schema-bridge-smoke.
Add a lightweight dashboard tile (Console QA) summarizing daily pass rate by model variant and the top 10 failing prompts.

2026-03-12 - Miguel Torres: Added CI shim and CLI wrapper. Opened PR #4281 for harness and validator integration. Marking blocked on infra ticket ENG-730112 for temporary test-bucket ACLs (now resolved).

risks: If CI time exceeds budget, we may need to reduce permutations (model x loss rates) which could hide model-specific regressions.
Quantized models may exhibit systematic trailing-token drops that require model-side fixes; smoke tests will surface but cannot automatically remediate.
False positives from overly strict validator: need to separate parser-level errors from generation-quality issues to avoid noisy alerts.
notes: Runner implementation should avoid heavyweight dependencies; use existing infra SDKs and the 'stream-replay' helper already in runtime/tests.
Where possible, reuse prompts and fixtures from ENG-42756 and ENG-14266 but re-label as 'smoke' so CI retention is minimized.
Follow-up epics anticipated: (a) schema-repair-orchestrator to attempt automated fixes on PARTIAL_FAILs, (b) extended fuzzing harness for relaxed-schema scenarios.
